newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's forint eases vs dollar on mark weakness.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's forint eases vs dollar on mark weakness.

text.p: Hungary's forint extended its losses against the dollar in early trading on Wednesday on the U.S. unit's rise against the mark, but remained steady against the central bank currency basket, dealers said.
"We rose back to the NBH bid (National Bank of Hungary resistance level) yesterday and we do not expect a change," said Robert Szucs of Inter-Europa Bank.
The forint opened at 194.57/62 to the dollar and slid to 195.09/14 by 0805 GMT, compared with Tuesday's close of 193.90/95, as the mark's fall against the dollar continued.
But the forint remained strong against the NBH currency basket, made up 30 percent of the dollar and 70 percent of the mark, trading at its accustomed position right at the NBH bid.

In the past two weeks the forint has drifted away from the NBH bid several times because of what dealers said was investors' uncertainty caused by floods and trade account problems in the Czech Republic and Poland.
"But not much capital has been withdrawn from Hungary, otherwise the forint would still be below the NBH bid by 30 to 50 fillers," Szucs said.
